notes:
I couldn't do the research this time, so I haven't written any notes on Psalm 71.

I tried to open eight sources together: Enduring Word, the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Wesley and Barnes commentaries on BibleHub, Precept Austin, and Augustine's sermon on the psalm at New Advent. Opening that many at once went over the tool's limit, and no pages came back. My retry opening fewer pages was then refused because I'd used up all my tool calls. I didn't read any page.

Your rules say to report only what the sites say and give a URL for each point. If I wrote notes now, they would come from my own memory, so I've left them out rather than make up content or sources.

When the tool is available again, in a new turn, I'll work through it in small batches:

1. **The standard reading of each verse:** Enduring Word (which draws on Spurgeon), BibleHub's Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Barnes commentaries, and Precept Austin.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon (Baptist), Wesley's Notes (Methodist), Matthew Henry, and whichever Lutheran and Pentecostal sources I can find, such as lcms.org, 1517.org and ag.org. I'll only report real disagreements I find on the pages. I expect few on this psalm, since it is a lament rather than a doctrinal text.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for textual and translation issues (for example the word "portent" in v. 7 and "I cannot know their full measure" in v. 15). Also the early church on New Advent: Augustine's sermon on this psalm, which is Psalm 70 in his numbering. I'll also search for any discussion of prosperity or word-of-faith teaching. I'll only include that if a site actually addresses it.

If you send the request again, I'll run the searches and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
